anil: Heads up - after the 03:14 deploy we're seeing 99p tail spikes on a subset of EU2 dedicated slices. Metric: p99_latency_tokens increased from ~210ms -> ~480ms for small-gen requests.
carla: ugh. any noisy neighbor traces?
san: infra-bot flagged a cross-tenant egress burst on rack-r23 around the same time.
infra-bot: ALERT: egress_burst_detected rack=r23 tenants=[tenant-442, tenant-811] window=30s peak_bytes=420MB/s
jess: copying the perf spike trace: 
```
[2026-03-19T03:14:12Z] alloc_id=ded-slice-77 tenant=tenant-442 reqs=124 p50=180ms p95=310ms p99=472ms
[2026-03-19T03:14:13Z] alloc_id=ded-slice-77 net_out=380MB/s tcp_q=87
```
carla: looks like NVLink/PCIe interconnect saturation + egress shaping hitting kernel qlen. Could be tenant-442 doing large embedding batches.
anil: tenant-442 is on Dedicated standard (reserved) - we can't casually preempt. We need an escape plan that doesn't violate SLA. Options: 1) route noisy flows to a soft-burst lane (isolated egress buffer) 2) temporarily move noisy tenant to fractional-dedicated slice (if available) 3) activate cross-region fallback to another eu2 rack (higher cost)
sam: OTOH, fallback to another rack costs ~0.6c/s and adds ~40-80ms. For this customer that latency might be OK for embeddings, but not for chat.
carla: what about switching tenant to quantized model variant (smaller mem footprint) as a graceful degradation? That reduces egress + NVLink pressure.
ops-oncall: we can toggle quantized fallback per-route, but we need approval from product for quality regression. Also need a routing policy change to allow short-lived regional handoffs without tenant consent.
anil: propose hybrid: enact egress headroom credits for each rack (bucket per-tenant) and when burst exceeds threshold we 1) throttle non-SLA traffic, 2) signal tenant to switch to quantized variant via header, 3) as last resort, failover to dedicated escape rack with traffic mirroring to avoid cold start.
sam: can we implement crediting as a controller change? rough sketch: grant 10GB burst tokens per tenant per-24h; tokens consumed by egress_mb above baseline; controller-metrics expose tokens_left. If tokens==0 then route to soft-burst lane (degraded but contained).
carla: sounds reasonable. Need cost model: what's customer-visible billing if we move to escape rack? also how many tokens to avoid frequent handoffs?
anil: quick calc: escape rack egress delta ~ +$0.15/hr for sustained burst vs baseline. Tokens should be sized to cover normal daily peaks - initial guess 10GB/day per tenant (subject to telemetry).
ops-oncall: I'll run a quick canary in eu2 rack-r23 with a small set of noisy tenants tonight. I'll add telemetry for token burn-rate and p99 delta.
jess: add a note to the playbook: when token burn rate > 2GB/10min, ops gets paged. Action items: ops-oncall will canary; sam to add controller PR sketch for token accounting; carla to draft quantized-variant fallback docs for product review.
anil: thanks. If canary goes well we'll roll policy out as an opt-in for Dedicated customers over the next week. :thumbsup:
